We show that an ensemble of a number of different models can bring down perplexity on this task to 23.7, a large improvement compared to current state-of-art.
The model was evaluated on small-scale language modeling experiments for various languages and matched the best results on the PTB data set despite having 60% fewer parameters.
The data set contains about 0.8B words with a vocabulary of 793471 words, including sentence boundary markers.
The words that are out of vocabulary (OOV) are marked with a special UNK token (there are approximately 0.3% such words).
The biases of LSTM forget gate were initialized to 1.0 .
The models were trained until convergence with an AdaGrad optimizer using a learning rate of 0.2.

Exhaustively trying all combinations would be extremely time consuming for such a large data set, but our findings suggest that LSTMs with a projection layer (i.e., a bottleneck between hidden states as in ) trained with truncated BPTT for 20 steps performed well.
In all the experiments the RNNs were unrolled for 20 steps without ever resetting the LSTM states.
Unless otherwise stated, the experiments were performed with 32 GPU workers and asynchronous gradient updates.
Most of the parameters are in the linear layer before the Softmax: 820M versus a total of 1.04B parameters.
